description: Hi! I'm a student passionate about space exploration, astronomy, coding, AI, and game development. I enjoy creating interactive websites, games, and simulations while learning new technologies. I'm joining the NASA Space Apps Challenge to collaborate, explore creative ideas, and solve real-world problems. I'm looking for teammates skilled in programming, UI/UX design, astronomy, research, 3D modeling, and presentations. Let's work together to create something innovative and inspiring! 🚀🌌
summary: Our team took on the challenge Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map and built a Martian map atlas website as our solution. The atlas brings together every location we explored on Mars, showing each site on an interactive map with key details such as terrain, elevation, temperature, radiation exposure, and access to resources like water ice. Alongside the map, we created a survival guide that ranks each location by its survival rate, based on factors like water availability, dust storms, radiation, atmospheric pressure, and how easy it would be to land, build shelter, and generate power. Our goal was to help people understand how harsh the Martian environment is and what it would take to survive there. By comparing locations side by side, users can see why some areas, such as low-lying regions with subsurface ice, are far safer than exposed, high-altitude zones. The website turns complex scientific data into a clear, engaging, and educational experience for students, space enthusiasts, and anyone curious about how future explorers might choose a landing site and prepare for life on another planet.

Project Description: Mars Explorer

Team Zenova-X | Interactive Mars Map and Survival Guide

Our project, Mars Explorer, is an interactive educational website designed to help people explore Mars, understand its environment, and learn what it might take for humans to survive there in the future. It uses real data from NASA's Mars Trek to create an engaging experience where users can explore the planet through interactive 2D maps, 3D models, spacecraft simulations, and a survival guide.

1. What does the project do and how does it work?

Mars Explorer allows users to explore the Red Planet in an interactive way. Instead of simply reading information about Mars, users can interact with maps, rotate 3D models, zoom into different locations, and discover important landmarks.

Some of its main features include:

  • Interactive 2D map: Allows users to pan and zoom across Mars using different map layers, including satellite imagery, topography, geology, and shaded relief.
  • 3D Mars model: Allows users to rotate a 3D model of Mars and explore 14 important geographical landmarks.
  • Spacecraft hangar: Displays 18 NASA spacecraft and vehicles, including rovers, landers, and orbiters, at realistic sizes.
  • Survival guide: Includes a clickable spacesuit, emergency procedures, a packing checklist, and important information about surviving on Mars.
  • Survival ranking: Compares different locations based on water availability, energy resources, radiation protection, shelter, and terrain.
  • Measurement tools: Allows users to measure distances between locations and explore elevation differences.

2. What benefits does the project have?

Our project has several educational and practical benefits:

  • Improves scientific knowledge: Helps users understand Mars's geography, atmosphere, climate, and environment.
  • Makes learning interactive: Allows students to explore information themselves instead of only reading textbooks.
  • Encourages critical thinking: Challenges users to consider which locations would be suitable for future human exploration.
  • Raises awareness of space exploration: Introduces users to NASA missions, spacecraft, and discoveries.
  • Develops problem-solving skills: The survival guide encourages users to think about the challenges astronauts might face on Mars.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

The main goal of Mars Explorer is to make space science more accessible, interesting, and understandable.

We want to encourage students and other users to become more interested in astronomy, technology, engineering, and scientific research. We also hope to help people understand the difficulties of future Mars missions, including limited resources, extreme temperatures, radiation, and the challenges of finding suitable locations for human settlements.

Ultimately, our project aims to inspire curiosity about space exploration and encourage the next generation to think about humanity's future beyond Earth.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

We developed the project as a web-based application using:

  • HTML: Used to structure the website and organise its different sections and features.
  • CSS: Used to design the website's appearance, including its colours, layouts, animations, and responsive design.
  • JavaScript: Used to create interactive features, calculations, animations, map controls, and other dynamic elements.
  • NASA Mars Trek: Provides publicly available Mars imagery and geographical data.
  • USGS and Arizona State University data: Credited as additional sources of imagery and scientific information.

The project uses web technologies such as HTML Canvas, SVG graphics, and JavaScript-based rendering to display visual elements and interactive planetary models.

The uploaded project is a web-based HTML application. No specific physical hardware or development software is identified in the project file.

5. How is your project creative?

Our project is creative because it combines science, technology, education, and interactive design into one platform.

Rather than creating a traditional informational website, we designed an experience that makes users feel as though they are exploring Mars themselves.

Some of our creative elements include:

  • A rotating, animated Mars model.
  • Interactive 2D and 3D planetary exploration.
  • Realistic spacecraft models displayed at their actual sizes.
  • A survival guide that introduces real challenges of living on Mars.
  • A survival ranking system that compares different locations.
  • Animated backgrounds, planetary effects, and a space-inspired visual design.

We also combined scientific information with interactive activities to make learning more enjoyable and memorable.

6. What factors did your team consider?

While developing Mars Explorer, our team considered several important factors:

  1. Scientific accuracy: We wanted to use real Mars data and reliable sources, particularly NASA.
  2. User experience: We designed the website so users could easily navigate between its different features.
  3. Educational value: We made sure the project provided useful scientific information rather than just visual entertainment.
  4. Creativity and innovation: We wanted to create something more interesting than a standard informational website.
  5. Accessibility: We considered different screen sizes, mobile devices, readable text, and reduced-motion settings.
  6. Technical performance: We considered loading times, animations, map rendering, and the performance of interactive features.
  7. Future exploration: We included factors such as water, energy, radiation protection, shelter, and terrain when considering potential human survival locations.

Conclusion

Mars Explorer represents our team's effort to combine creativity, scientific research, and programming to create an educational space exploration platform. By bringing together interactive maps, 3D models, NASA data, and a survival guide, we have developed a project that allows users to discover Mars in an engaging and informative way.

Our ultimate ambition is to inspire people to learn more about space, understand the challenges of exploring other planets, and imagine what the future of human exploration could look like.

Team Zenova-X 🚀
